title: 2.5D RPG: Fixed camera or player-controlled rotation?
author: AkiraVero
selftext:
Hi all! My fiancee and I are making a Cozy / Hardcore 2.5D Pixel MMORPG and we're deciding whether to keep our rotating camera or just use a static camera.

Having a rotating camera has been a lot of extra work making scenery / props / trying to make them look good from every angle. But on the other hand, we feel like if done right and the effort is put into polishing it, it could look great and add a lot more to the game and make the world feel more alive.

I uploaded a small clip from a demo we are putting together of a short combat scene and a short rotation at the end with a Fixed Camera vs one with a player turning the camera. It may be difficult to judge from just the short clip, but any feedback in general is greatly appreciated.

  
What do you guys think? Any and all feedback (even if not about the camera) is greatly appreciated!

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body: love this look, nice work on the style and graphics

comments.author: HitMePat
comments.body: The fact that the camera rotation looks so clean means you should definitely use it.  Only reason to have a fixed camera IMO is if you don't want to do the work to make it look good from every direction.  But you already did.

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: Thank you for that. We are both very analytical and a lot of our back and forth is because we are nitpicking at small details that probably don't need to be absolutely perfect right now and can be refined later.

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body:
Im on both sides of this fence and I hope it doesnt make it more difficult for you. 

1. I like how mobas do not have rotational cameras, it helps with memorizing the map etc, and it makes it "reliable". I suspect that this also makes building / prototyping easier and assets largely remain 2d.

2. the rotation does look smooth, it feels good, but how does that affect your models? I assume this makes them all need depth etc, im not entirely sure if that is coming at an additional cost to you, but i suspect it will make building everything more complex. If it doesnt then I would say keep it, the more viewing angles the more options. Though my concern would come from the added complexity that it is bringing (scope creep) vs what the goal is. 

What does your asset funnel look like? they seem to be 3d here at least (front / back / sides) hence the ask.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
I'd say fixed camera. It's mostly a 2D game even if you made it in 3D. In some games like Fez the camera rotation is part of the core mechanic, but for your game I don't think it is.

It looks very clean, but that should not be a reason to use it.

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: Thank you. So conflicted still. Even if the assets are in 3D and we have the ability to rotate the camera, if we are not really putting it to good use, is the effort worth it? I'm not sure we can justify it unless we actually put some thought into how we can utilize it properly. Right now there are no mechanics tied to it and it's just a pure style choice.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: You already did the effort. It works, it looks good, but it's unnecessary. So don't use it.

comments.author: fued
comments.body:
i dunno if player rotation is good. having it auto rotate on bosses/target could work tho.

people just wont really rotate unless they want to see something/somethings blocked

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: Yep. We have noticed that as-well and we see ourselves doing that. Really good point. When we are playing through our demo most of the time we don't even rotate the camera ourselves unless it's for testing it. I think you also have another good point that we haven't really thought about - auto rotation during certain content could still be viable. For example in our game we have like Monster Races and a few in-game "cinematic" shots that utilize the rotation. Maybe it can still be a part of the game, but just tailored. Thank you for that.

comments.author: TrashCollector1337
comments.body: I believe the camera is fine as is, I like it

comments.author: Direy_Cupcake
comments.body: Player-controlled rotation looks way too good. Im honestly surprised nobody liked it. The world looks lively with it

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: Rotate...why because lazy ai devs wont do it ...your game instantly shines

comments.author: StellarAmazoniansDev
comments.body: Given the type of game, I think you could implement automatic camera rotation—where the game controls the angle based on your location on the map, rather than the player doing it. For instance, if a large enemy appears, the camera could rotate to focus on it. If you leave camera control up to the player, they’ll likely only adjust it when it’s strictly necessary to progress or discover something.
